entries.sanskrit:
चतुस्त्रिंशेऽहिना ग्रस्तं नन्दं हरिर् अमूमुचत् ।

विद्याध्रं चाङ्गिरः-शापाच् छङ्खचूडं तथावधीत् ॥

रासापदेशतः कामं किङ्करी-कृत्य कामतः ।

अनुगृह्णन् वशं निन्ये तथा विद्याधराधिपम् ॥

तद् एवं कामानुग्रह-मुखेन काम-जयं प्रतिपाद्य तथैव विद्याधर-जयं प्रतिपादयितुं तत् प्रसङ्गं दर्शयति---एकदा इति ॥१.२॥
entries.literal_english: At the beginning of the Thirty-fourth Chapter, Śrīdhara states that Hari freed Nanda from the serpent and also killed Śaṅkhacūḍa, the Vidyādhara cursed by the Āṅgirasa sages.
entries.source_note: The supplied Śrīdhara source block spans 10.34.1–10.34.2 and is repeated unchanged in the verse-level reader records.

entries.sanskrit: गोपेष्व् आत्मन ऐश्वर्यं प्रकाशयितुम् अविद्वान् इव तम् अपृच्छत् । दीप्यमानेन वपुषा समवस्थितम् ॥१०॥
entries.literal_english: Kṛṣṇa asked the liberated being about his identity while appearing to reveal His majesty among the cowherds as though He did not know it; the man stood in a radiant divine body.

entries.sanskrit: यः परया शोभया प्रकाशते भवान् क इति ॥११.१२॥
entries.literal_english: Kṛṣṇa asks who the wonderfully radiant person is and how he was forced into such a despised condition.

entries.sanskrit:
अहि-देहं निहत्यैवं प्राग् उन्मत्तं सुदर्शनम् ।

तद्वद् उन्मादिनं कृष्णं शङ्खचूडम् अताडयत् ॥

तत्-प्रसङ्गम् आह---कदाचिद् इति ॥२०॥
entries.literal_english: Śrīdhara connects this event with the earlier release of Sudarśana: just as Kṛṣṇa struck the former mad serpent-form, He now struck the mad Śaṅkhacūḍa.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, निशा-प्रवेशं सत्-कुर्वन्तौ । उदित उडुपस् तारकाश् च यस्मिंस् तत् । मल्लिका-गन्धेन मत्ता अलयो यस्मिंस् तत् ॥२२॥
word_for_word: making the entrance of night auspicious
when the moon and stars had risen
entries.literal_english: The night became auspicious as the moon and stars rose, and the grove was filled with bees intoxicated by the fragrance of jasmine.

entries.sanskrit: अनिबद्धत्वाद् अन्यैर् युगपत् कल्पयितुम् अशक्यम् अपि तौ स्वर-मण्डलस्य मूर्च्छितं युगपत् कल्पयन्तौ । मनः-श्रवणयोर् मङ्गलं यथा भवति तथा जगतुर् अगायताम् इति ॥२३॥
word_for_word: impossible for others to produce simultaneously
the melodic convergence of the scale
entries.literal_english: The two Lords sang in simultaneous melodic patterns that others could not produce together, making the music auspicious and pleasing to both mind and ear.
